Sentence (English): Three years ago we purchased a Bosch dishwasher for our vacation home -- which we absolutely love.
Comments (English): [ Great hardware. Software -- not so much. ] || ---------------- || Three years ago we purchased a Bosch dishwasher for our vacation home -- which we absolutely love. It's quiet, efficient and has a very well thought out design. So when it came time to replace the dishwasher in our family home, the decision was easy -- another Bosch dishwasher! And as far as the hardware goes, this one is just as nice. However we've found this new one to be significantly harder to program. Unless you install and use the phone App and connect the dishwasher to your wifi network, trying to do something that should be simple (like set the auto dry function) is ridiculously complex. It requires you to perform an exacting sequence of button pushes which is impossible to figure out without consulting the user manual. And even then the directions are so arcane that it took me multiple tries to get it right. But if you're ok whipping out your phone every time you want to change a setting on your dishwasher then maybe this isn't an issue for you. It was for me, so I docked it one star. One other minor issue is that the silverware basket on this newer model is half the size of our older one (! ). Too small! I guess they want you to encourage putting your silverware on the top rack. However our top rack is usually filled with larger utensils. So I had to buy a bigger silverware basket online to replace the one provided. Problem fixed (see photo)!

Cons: Bottom two racks aren't easy or intuitive to load (internet research hasn't helped). Doesn't get dishes as clean, often a bowl or cup comes out dirty after the cycle, although I'm careful not to block the sprayers when I load it. Also, there's no way to choose a default preference, if you don't want heat dry to run during the cycle you have to turn it off every time. Maybe the worst thing: it's smelly. I scrape the dishes to make sure there aren't any large food bits to clog the drain, and clean the filter often, but it always has a slightly fishy odor. It works OK, maybe not worth the hassle of returning and purchasing another one, I'd give it 2.5 stars if they let me do a half star. Definitely would not purchase again.

Due to the light weight of the door you have to push the door down with effort to get the bottom rack out. The Dish rack on the bottom has a weird organization style and doesn't fit my dishes well. The vent in the top left of the door is a bad design element and leaks on the floor every single time you have the door fully open which is not good for wood floors. Overall not a bad dishwasher for the price point but in the end you get what you pay for. The higher priced models from other brands have much more to offer and will last longer than this dishwasher.

When I removed the new filter I installed I could tell the water was dripping from the plunger/nozzle on the filter housing. Not enough to give any warning at the time of the replacement of the filter. As evident with the numerous bad reviews there seems to be a design flaw or just plain bad engineering with the filtration system. I would highly recommend staying away from Samsung Refrigerators.

Sentence (English): I turned it on at night and checked in the morning that there was a little moisture because it had dried naturally with the automatic door opening function.
Comments (English): [ The groom made a pedestal to store detergent underneath, and it's perfect! ] || ---------------- || I turned it on at night and checked in the morning that there was a little moisture because it had dried naturally with the automatic door opening function. It would be better if you took it out from the bottom and organized the top. It was difficult to play Tetris for the first time. The small pillars on the tray don't move, so it takes some getting used to. The shape of the bowls, pot lids, bath lids, and broth strainers caused a lot of water to accumulate. I put them in the dishwasher and re-dried them. Since I have an ultrasonic washer and a dishwasher, I am very satisfied with the dishwasher that is faithful to the basic functions such as washing and rinsing. I intentionally took a picture of the inside after organizing the dishes. This much moisture remained the next day, and if you expect more water to accumulate depending on the shape or arrangement of the dishes, you won't be disappointed. I find it more convenient when the dryer, dishwasher, and ultrasonic cleaner are arranged at a similar height! And because the washer is raised, it's easier to drain. It's a whole new world. I hope everyone raises their heads and gets rid of back pain.
Comments (Original): [ 신랑이 받침대를 짜서 밑에 세제 수납하니 완전 굿! ] || ---------------- || 밤에 돌리고 아침에 보니 자동문열림 기능으로 자연 건조라 물기가 조금 있었어요.하단부터 빼고 상단을 정리하면 좀 낫겠죠.첫 사용이라 테트리스가 어려웠어요.트레이에 있는 작은 기둥들이 움직이는게 아니라서 적응이 필요하겠어요.그릇,냄비 뚜껑,바트 뚜껑,육수망 같은 것은 모양 때문에 물이 제법 고여있습니다.원래 있던 식기건조기에 넣고 다시 재건조 시켰습니다.초음파세척기,식기건조기가 있어서 세척,헹굼같은 기본 기능에 충실한 세척기로는 아주 만족합니다.어차피 식기세척기로 모든 설거지를 할 수 없기때문에 적당한 가격선에서 잘 샀습니다.일시정지 기능이 있어서 빠진 소서 넣고 어찌나 뿌듯하던지... 아침에 반짝반짝 그릇을 보니까 기분이 너무 좋더군요.세탁기도 저는 일체형보단 건조기 따로 있는 것이 더 효율적이다 생각하기 때문에 그릇 특성 상관없이 마구 넣기엔 세척,헹굼 온도가 50~65도,잔열 건조 75도 밖에 안되는 이 세척기가 최고네요.^^다만 주방공간 제약있으신 분들은 건조때문에 신경쓰이지 않을까 싶습니다.일부러 그릇정리후 남은 내부 사진을 찍었습니다.이 정도 물기가 이튿날 남아있고 그릇 모양이나 배열에 따라 물이 더 고여있다고 예상하시면 실망하실 일은 없을 것 같습니다.저는 건조기,식기세척기,초음파세척기가 비슷한 높이에  배열되니 더 편하네요!!!!그리고 세척기를 올렸기 때문에 배수에 더 용이한 점도 있고,완전 새로운 세상입니다.다들 올려서 허리통증에서 해방되시길 바랍니다.

Comments (Original): [ 신랑이 받침대를 짜서 밑에 세제 수납하니 완전 굿! ] || ---------------- || 밤에 돌리고 아침에 보니 자동문열림 기능으로 자연 건조라 물기가 조금 있었어요.하단부터 빼고 상단을 정리하면 좀 낫겠죠.첫 사용이라 테트리스가 어려웠어요.트레이에 있는 작은 기둥들이 움직이는게 아니라서 적응이 필요하겠어요.그릇,냄비 뚜껑,바트 뚜껑,육수망 같은 것은 모양 때문에 물이 제법 고여있습니다.원래 있던 식기건조기에 넣고 다시 재건조 시켰습니다.초음파세척기,식기건조기가 있어서 세척,헹굼같은 기본 기능에 충실한 세척기로는 아주 만족합니다.어차피 식기세척기로 모든 설거지를 할 수 없기때문에 적당한 가격선에서 잘 샀습니다.일시정지 기능이 있어서 빠진 소서 넣고 어찌나 뿌듯하던지... 아침에 반짝반짝 그릇을 보니까 기분이 너무 좋더군요.세탁기도 저는 일체형보단 건조기 따로 있는 것이 더 효율적이다 생각하기 때문에 그릇 특성 상관없이 마구 넣기엔 세척,헹굼 온도가 50~65도,잔열 건조 75도 밖에 안되는 이 세척기가 최고네요.^^다만 주방공간 제약있으신 분들은 건조때문에 신경쓰이지 않을까 싶습니다.일부러 그릇정리후 남은 내부 사진을 찍었습니다.이 정도 물기가 이튿날 남아있고 그릇 모양이나 배열에 따라 물이 더 고여있다고 예상하시면 실망하실 일은 없을 것 같습니다.저는 건조기,식기세척기,초음파세척기가 비슷한 높이에  배열되니 더 편하네요!!!!그리고 세척기를 올렸기 때문에 배수에 더 용이한 점도 있고,완전 새로운 세상입니다.다들 올려서 허리통증에서 해방되시길 바랍니다.

Sentence (English): Oh~!
Comments (English): Oh~! I've never used Samsung! Most of the home appliances I use at home are LG, and as for the dishwasher, I have only used LG dishwashers, so I really thought a lot about whether to get Samsung or LG home appliances until the very end. This is why the experience is so important, so I ended up going with LG. I haven't used Samsung, but it's one of the home appliances I use that I'm really satisfied with! The steam course is also good, so it really cleans and disinfects stuck food! The reason I decided to choose LG was because I happened to have the opportunity to try out a Miele dishwasher and I really liked it. I felt that the ease of use was definitely LG. The basket seemed to be similar, but it was easy to place, and strangely, the dishwasher I used did not have an automatic door opening (Miele product), so I went with LG for a few reasons! I think it’s best to do something you’re familiar with! However, if you ask about my experience with the LG dishwasher, I wash the pot well too! I never once felt like it wasn't cleaned properly, and because of that clean feeling, I even use the dishwasher to wash the tumblers and cups once in a while! Milk drinking cups and cups with a fishy smell are all solved~! This is a very satisfying home appliance.

I would love for it to be able to do delay start (have it set to start at midnight so that it washes and dries when we are sleeping or when the energy grid is not really in high demand). Other than an app that doesn't seem to really do anything, no complaints.

Tech came before agreed estimate, and was very efficient in installation. He was in and out in 1 hour, and hauled away our broken and stinky old dishwasher. So far, it's been 2 months since the install and we couldn't be happier with this model. Why did we choose this over the Bosch? Primarily because of the 3rd rack and that we were very happy with the previous KitchenAid. Highly recommend this dishwasher model.

Sentence (English): I received a KitchenAid 44 DBA Dishwasher, equipped with a FreeFlex Third Rack and LED Interior Lighting, complimentary from KitchenAid and Influenster in exchange for my honest review.
Comments (English): [ Modern, Spacious, Durable, and Superior Performance! ] || ---------------- || I received a KitchenAid 44 DBA Dishwasher, equipped with a FreeFlex Third Rack and LED Interior Lighting, complimentary from KitchenAid and Influenster in exchange for my honest review. The KitchenAid 44 DBA Dishwasher, with FreeFlex Third Rack and LED Interior Lighting adds a whole new dimension to my kitchen, by adding an industrial look with a modern vibe. The stainless steel PrintShield finish keeps the dishwasher looking clean and smudge-free, which is great feature, especially when you have little ones running around touching everything! The outside is easy to clean with just a water-dampened cloth, and is resistant to scratching. The gorgeous and functional stainless steel handle is both sturdy and strong, and doesn't loosen with repetitive pulling. Also located on the front door, just above the handle on the right-hand side, is a tiny light that changes color to show how much time is left in the dishwasher's cleaning cycle. The operating panel is located discreetly at the top of the dishwasher, so the front remains smooth, sleek, and clean. The panel is digital and features (Cycles) Pro Wash, Tough, Express, and Rinse Wash on the left side of the time panel, and (Options) Hi-Temp, Sani-Rinse, Pro Dry, Top 2-Racks, and Time-Delay on the right side. The Start and Cancel buttons are on the right side of the time panel as well. THE INSIDE! I can seriously fit my whole kitchen inside this dishwasher and still have room for more; yes, it is that roomy! Inside, there are THREE slide-out racks for endless loading possibilities, each with its own separate jet system for complete and absolute cleaning power. I found the top rack ideal for my bowls, bottles, glasses, mugs, and both cooking and eating utensils. The (second) middle row is perfect for my pots, larger bowls, dishes, and such, and the bottom is for just about everything else, like plates and oblong platters. I love how the racks are adjustable to fit just about anything imaginable. The LED lighting inside is so bright, and so beautiful. It makes the entire stainless steel interior light up so I can easily see everything inside. I also love that unlike my older plastic interior dishwasher, the KitchenAid stainless steel interior won't stain or pick up odors. I LOVE the Pro Dry Cycle! I don't have to worry any longer with wet dripping plastic ware or puddles on the tops of my mugs. The Pro Dry cycle let's me add an additional 15 minutes of drying time to my load if my dishes are still slightly wet. I really appreciate that there's an Express Wash. The cycle is super fast, super-duper quiet, and my dishes come out ultra clean and spotless. The KitchenAid 44 DBA Dishwasher with FreeFlex Third Rack and LED Interior Lighting, is perfect for our busy and constantly on-the-go family. It's durable, sturdy, and by the quality, I can tell it'll last our family a very long time!

Sentence (English): This dishwasher by LG looks fantastic!
Comments (English): [ This dishwasher is a high-performing appliance that surpassed my expectations. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher by LG looks fantastic! It performs exceptionally well with minimal noise. During my testing, I used glass cookware for baking brownies and some air fryer parts for making burgers. After a light rinse to remove loose debris, I loaded the dishwasher, downloaded the P4 cycle (pot & pans) in the app, and started the cycle. To my delight, everything emerged spotless (before and after photos available), without any residues to scrape or scrub. The 13x9 glass bakeware sat perfectly on the lower rack, securely holding it in place and allowing efficient water drainage. The dishwasher's jets exhibit remarkable power; the audible water pressure during operation is a clear testament to this. I love the ability to open and close the door without activating/powering on the appliance is a simple yet appreciated feature. The top display has an impressive finish, although I suggest the inclusion of a back-lit display with adjustable brightness levels for enhanced visibility in varying lighting conditions. The racks are not only robust but also designed for seamless functionality. Their smooth gliding, user-friendly handles, and easily accessible thumb releases make loading and unloading a breeze. When raising or lowering the upper rack it works great and locks in place in designated zones to line up with the water supply on the back wall of the dishwasher. The racks also feature fold-down dish holders for accommodating larger items and silverware holder tops that open to accommodate bulkier utensils. The removable silverware holder is a thoughtful addition, and the small holes prevent items from interfering with the rinse arms. The efficient design of the heating and venting system ensures a thorough drying process. While the dishwasher generally delivers exceptional cleaning and drying results, there are occasional water puddles on items such as the bottom of a coffee mug. The vent/exhaust port is on the bottom of the door (left side). The design of the lower arms holes and jets are strategically positioned to tackle heavily soiled items. Moreover, the appliance's cleaning and maintenance tasks, including filter cleaning, are made effortless with a guide indicating when and how to perform these essential upkeep steps. The LG ThinQ app is easy to use & can do many cool things. You choose your cycle on the app, press Download Cycle on the dishwasher panel then start & you're all set. You should check it out! I can auto-start items based on the weather, time, and location. There is a Clean Coach that tells you when and how to clean the machine, Energy monitoring, and much more. In conclusion, this dishwasher is a high-performing appliance that surpassed my expectations. I would wholeheartedly recommend this product without hesitation! 5 stars!

Sentence (English): I replaced my 20 year old Frigidaire dishwasher with this one a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and efficient ] || ---------------- || I replaced my 20 year old Frigidaire dishwasher with this one a month ago. Keep in mind that we have off the scale hard water, so I do need a robust dishwasher. I'm impressed with the new one. I no longer have to fully clean each dish before loading into the dishwasher. Because of the hard water I have to use Lemishine crystals in the open basket and I now need a lot less of them. I tried a couple of the cycles and found the normal with heat dry is fine for most days. I have never had such clean smelling dishes and dishwasher! My installer advised that I need to use powdered detergent but it's impossible to find. I have been using Cascade pods that have both Dawn and Oxi in them. I haven't found a single item that did not come out perfect. You can feel the difference on the silverware. Very pleasantly surprised!

Some math-geek probably calculated you could squeeze in 3 more forks this way, but it's all downsides otherwise. 2. the 2 wire racks on the bottom and bottom that are adjustable are nice, and adjustable. Generally, the wire rack width and alignment in this machine isn't well positioned like the last few machines we have used so there is wasted space all over. 3. Sentence (English): We've had this dishwasher for approximately one year.
Comments (English): [ It\u2019s probably best to pre-rinse dishes ] || ---------------- || We've had this dishwasher for approximately one year. We were replacing it with a KitchenAid that was approximately 13 years old. What I liked about the previous KitchenAid, and about my dishwasher prior to that (not a KitchenAid) was that I never had to prerinse my dishes. I would scrape the food off and load, the dishes into the dishwasher, where they often sat for a few days before running the dishwasher, and everything would come out clean 99% of the time. I assumed this would be the same but it's not. I must pre-rinse many of the dishes now and have probably found more things that did not come clean in the year that I've had it, than I did the entire time I had the previous dishwasher. I'm not a huge fan of the third rack, simply because it leaves, less room for very large items on the middle shelf. Although the middle shelf is adjustable by one notch (up or down), taking it down means my very tall cutting board on the bottom shelf won't fit. I Would say about one out of every five loads has something that was missed, that I then need to wash by hand. That is my biggest complaint. Other than that, it is a very quiet dishwasher, which I completely appreciate!

But I have no issue with the time for my needs.

Sentence (English): This replaces a 19 year old Kenmore dishwasher that was purchased in 2005, unfortunately the part we needed was no longer made.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and mostly what I wanted in a dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This replaces a 19 year old Kenmore dishwasher that was purchased in 2005, unfortunately the part we needed was no longer made. The new replacement Kitchen Aid met most of my requirements; however, I've only used it twice so the review may change as time goes by. The things I wanted and why: there is no 3rd rack which are worthless because most of them are to swallow, and yes, I've had plenty of experience with the 3rd rack that other people had. The forks, spoons, knives are on the side of the bottom rack and not in the door. This positioning does a better job of cleaning as well as being more convenient to load and unload. So far my glasses are sparkling clean with no white residue and I have not used the Finish Jet-Dry, which I never used in my old dishwasher and I believe if a dishwasher is quality there is no need for it. The test of time will see if this holds true on this new dishwasher! The cleaning selections are on the outside top front of the door which allows you to see where the unit is in the cleaning cycle. I prefer this placement over the cleaning selections that are on the inside top which you cannot see unless the door is open. The top rack adjusts up or down to accommodate larger items on either the bottom or top rack. The unit is super quiet and that's because there are no models made with food grinders anymore as far as I know. What I don't like: there is no food grinder so the dishes must be free of food particles; you do not have to prewash your dishes but you do need to scrape off the food pieces. At least once a month clean the filter which although inconvenient it is not hard to do. Next, when I lowered the top rack the button stuck down on one side so that I could not raise it back up. I was able to use a butter knife to pop it back in place which allowed me to raise the rack back up. Since I seldom raise or lower the rack I'm hoping this won't be a major issue!

Sentence (English): I used a 12-person model for a long time and switched to this one.
Comments (English): I used a 12-person model for a long time and switched to this one. It has many advantages. The 12-person model was not hygienic because dishes and food scraps were left in the sink all day until the dishes were collected, and it was quite annoying to bend down to put in and take out the dishes. Anyway, I have to wash the large dishes by hand. If I use it for a long time, the drain pipe gets clogged with foreign substances and I have to replace the drain pipe. This product solves these problems. It is better to take the drain pipe directly into the sink for later, and it seems more convenient to have the water supply pipe automatically supplied. There is no drying function, but I didn't use the drying function in the previous model. I'm afraid of the electricity bill, so just open the door slightly after washing. It's better to rinse the dried ingredients roughly before putting the dishes in. Don't put coated frying pans in because the coating will come off. My house's water bill is usually high, so I think it will be a big help in reducing the amount of hot water used. I'm very satisfied with the price, Coupang installation, and after-sales service! Anyway, it seems like domestic brands also produce OEM products from this company and just raise the price to sell them. I highly recommend it!

Sentence (English): This is a real review after using several dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a sincere review. ] || ---------------- || This is a real review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher and then downgraded to a 6-person one. Of course. It doesn't have the same cleaning power as a 12-person one. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of changing it to a detergent with better cleaning power. And Chefbon? I also used a 6-person dishwasher without installation, but what is this? It all falls under the dishes. It has to be placed tightly horizontally and vertically to put small dishes on it, but what the heck. There are only long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are too big, so rice bowls fall out. You only need to put in large dishes, but there's not enough space to put in large dishes. If you put in a large dish, it covers the detergent drawer door, so the detergent doesn't come out, or it pops out and the door doesn't close. Seriously. I wondered why they made it like this. In the end, I couldn't use it, so I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher. I found this Media product, and it seems to be the same as Cuckoo? The product size, weight, and basket shape are all the same, so it seems that Media sold Cuckoo, but Coupang directly imports and installs Media products. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and has 2 years of after-sales service for rocket installation. Cuckoo is about 250,000 won, and it is a little better if you connect to a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (they said that the phone call doesn't connect at all), but it is a 1:1 chat consultation, so you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is basic 1 year, but if you verify something on the official website, it is 1 year and 6 months? It is also difficult to call an installer every time. So I decided not to use Cuckoo and bought Media. Pros? It is cheap. Cons? It is cheap, but it is not cleaned well because there is no upper nozzle. I put all the frying pans and pots in it and turn it. (That's how I used the dishwasher until now) But since the water doesn't come out from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned well, and it doesn't clean every corner perfectly. The detergent is based on Frosch baking soda. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will do. You don't need to put in all of it. For 12 people, 1 Frosh is enough, and for 6 people, half is enough. If you put too much detergent, the water can smell.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong and I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that wouldn't come off no matter how hard you scrub will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the oily pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Shefubong is really inconvenient because the placement is fixed) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes in the upper left compartment won't be cleaned well, so you'll have to move them to the right or play Tetris well. Anyway, the cleaning power of the dishwasher is all similar, and the detergent determines it, but the lack of an upper nozzle definitely makes a difference in the cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you won't feel any discomfort at all. The inside is cleaned very well. (It's detergent anyway.) And those who turn it right away won't feel much inconvenience. Those who put it in a basket and turn it with oil all over the dishes or downgrade like me will probably say, "Hmm. It's a little less clean. When you touch it, the outside isn't very clean, but it doesn't feel like the dishes aren't washed. Anyway, it's bound to be cleaned better than hand washing. Well. I don't know if this media dishwasher with cascade will clean it very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. Chefbone was really annoying because of the fan noise when it was finished (the fan would automatically run for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; When I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after it was finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient). It’s actually better because there’s no such thing, and since I don’t need the automatic door-opening function, I usually open the door right after it’s finished to dry it. (If you shake off the accumulated water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they’re hot.) I’m not planning to use it for a long time, so I’m satisfied with it. For those who plan to use it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive, but considering the price, this product isn’t bad. If you spend more money on detergent, it seems like it’ll cover it to some extent~ And what goes in. It goes in as much as the size of the basket. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall bowls, so I don’t feel like it’s full. If you use a lot of flat bowls, it seems like it’ll really fit a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it’s more than half full. (There is a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser where dishes cannot be placed) but it definitely holds less than 12 people. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we rotate it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's true. When using it for 12 people, we soaked it in water and rotated it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals they eat a day, and since each household uses different sizes and numbers of dishes, roughly calculate how much dishes will come out and buy them. And I use thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stir-fry so they don't fall out easily, and both the frying pan and pot have Magic Hands? detachable handles, so I can load large frying pans and pots without any inconvenience. (Tefal is expensive, so I use the inexpensive Magic Hands product. I've had it for over a year, and the coating doesn't come off even if I run the dishwasher hard, so it's really good.) The perforation holes are 6mm. The installer was very kind and installed it very quickly. And when I used the Chefbone 6-person non-installation dishwasher, I bought a 20-liter water tank and used it, and since I am a person who does not feel that inconvenienced, I asked if I could use it in a water tank so as not to have to drill holes, and the technician said that it was not possible. If it was possible, I would have sold it as a non-installation dishwasher. Non-installation dishwashers have a function to suck up water, and this one should have water coming in automatically. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there, but I do not have a water purifier, so I drilled a hole in the marble top where it is not visible and connected it under the sink. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a sincere review. ] || ---------------- || This is a real review after using several dishwashers. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall bowls, so I don’t feel like it’s full. If you use a lot of flat bowls, it seems like it’ll really fit a lot. The perforation holes are 6mm. The installer was very kind and installed it very quickly. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a sincere review. ] || ---------------- || This is a real review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher and then downgraded to a 6-person one. Of course. It doesn't have the same cleaning power as a 12-person one. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of changing it to a detergent with better cleaning power. And Chefbon? I also used a 6-person dishwasher without installation, but what is this? It all falls under the dishes. It has to be placed tightly horizontally and vertically to put small dishes on it, but what the heck. There are only long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are too big, so rice bowls fall out. You only need to put in large dishes, but there's not enough space to put in large dishes. If you put in a large dish, it covers the detergent drawer door, so the detergent doesn't come out, or it pops out and the door doesn't close. Seriously. I wondered why they made it like this. In the end, I couldn't use it, so I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher. I found this Media product, and it seems to be the same as Cuckoo? The product size, weight, and basket shape are all the same, so it seems that Media sold Cuckoo, but Coupang directly imports and installs Media products. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and has 2 years of after-sales service for rocket installation. Cuckoo is about 250,000 won, and it is a little better if you connect to a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (they said that the phone call doesn't connect at all), but it is a 1:1 chat consultation, so you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is basic 1 year, but if you verify something on the official website, it is 1 year and 6 months? It is also difficult to call an installer every time. So I decided not to use Cuckoo and bought Media. Pros? It is cheap. Cons? It is cheap, but it is not cleaned well because there is no upper nozzle. I put all the frying pans and pots in it and turn it. (That's how I used the dishwasher until now) But since the water doesn't come out from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned well, and it doesn't clean every corner perfectly. The detergent is based on Frosch baking soda. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will do. You don't need to put in all of it. For 12 people, 1 Frosh is enough, and for 6 people, half is enough. If you put too much detergent, the water can smell.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong and I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that wouldn't come off no matter how hard you scrub will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the oily pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Shefubong is really inconvenient because the placement is fixed) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes in the upper left compartment won't be cleaned well, so you'll have to move them to the right or play Tetris well. Anyway, the cleaning power of the dishwasher is all similar, and the detergent determines it, but the lack of an upper nozzle definitely makes a difference in the cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you won't feel any discomfort at all. The inside is cleaned very well. (It's detergent anyway.) And those who turn it right away won't feel much inconvenience. Those who put it in a basket and turn it with oil all over the dishes or downgrade like me will probably say, "Hmm. It's a little less clean. When you touch it, the outside isn't very clean, but it doesn't feel like the dishes aren't washed. Anyway, it's bound to be cleaned better than hand washing. Well. I don't know if this media dishwasher with cascade will clean it very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. Chefbone was really annoying because of the fan noise when it was finished (the fan would automatically run for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; When I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after it was finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient). It’s actually better because there’s no such thing, and since I don’t need the automatic door-opening function, I usually open the door right after it’s finished to dry it. (If you shake off the accumulated water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they’re hot.) I’m not planning to use it for a long time, so I’m satisfied with it. For those who plan to use it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive, but considering the price, this product isn’t bad. If you spend more money on detergent, it seems like it’ll cover it to some extent~ And what goes in. It goes in as much as the size of the basket. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall bowls, so I don’t feel like it’s full. If you use a lot of flat bowls, it seems like it’ll really fit a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it’s more than half full. (There is a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser where dishes cannot be placed) but it definitely holds less than 12 people. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we rotate it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's true. When using it for 12 people, we soaked it in water and rotated it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals they eat a day, and since each household uses different sizes and numbers of dishes, roughly calculate how much dishes will come out and buy them. And I use thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stir-fry so they don't fall out easily, and both the frying pan and pot have Magic Hands? detachable handles, so I can load large frying pans and pots without any inconvenience. (Tefal is expensive, so I use the inexpensive Magic Hands product. I've had it for over a year, and the coating doesn't come off even if I run the dishwasher hard, so it's really good.) The perforation holes are 6mm. The installer was very kind and installed it very quickly. And when I used the Chefbone 6-person non-installation dishwasher, I bought a 20-liter water tank and used it, and since I am a person who does not feel that inconvenienced, I asked if I could use it in a water tank so as not to have to drill holes, and the technician said that it was not possible. If it was possible, I would have sold it as a non-installation dishwasher. Non-installation dishwashers have a function to suck up water, and this one should have water coming in automatically. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there, but I do not have a water purifier, so I drilled a hole in the marble top where it is not visible and connected it under the sink. When I asked about the time of dismantling it later, they kindly explained it to me. (수저통이 있고 세제 투입구 앞에는 그릇을 또 못놓은 공간이 조금 있어서) 확실히 12인용보다 적게 들어갑니다만...  2명이서 하루 세끼 집에서 밥 먹는데 하루 한 번 돌립니다만... 햇반 먹고 반찬도 안 먹어서 그렇긴 합니다.  12인용 쓸 때는 물에 담궈놓고 3일에 한번 돌렸어요. 몇인 가정이다 하루 몇끼 먹는다는 중요치 않은 것 같고 가정마다 사용하는 식기 크기와 개수가 다르기 때문에 식기가 얼마나 나오는지 대략 계산해보고 구매하세요.  그리고 저는 젓기릭을 다이소에 파는 통통한 젓가락을 사용해서 잘 안 빠지고 후라이팬과 냄비 모두 매직핸즈? 손잡이 탈부착 되는 걸로 사용해서 큰 후라이팬, 냄비도 불편함 없이 적재합니다. (테팔은 비싸서 저렴한 매직핸즈 제품 사용함ㅎ 1년 넘었는데 식세기 마구 돌려도 코팅 안 벗겨지고 아주 좋네요.)  타공 구멍은 6미리라고 합니다. 설치기사님 친절하고 아주 빠르게 설치하시고 가셨음.  그리고 저는 쉐프본 6인용 무설치 식세기 사용 할 때 20리터 물통 사놓고 담아서 썼고 그런 게 크게 불편하게 느껴지지 않는 사람이라 타공하지 않기 위해 물통에 받아서 쓸 수 있냐고 여쭤보니 기사님이 불가한 제품이라고 하셨어요.  만약 가능했다면 무설치 식세기로 팔았겠죠? 무설치 식세기들은 물을 빨아들이는 기능이 있는 걸테고 이 아이는 물이 자동으로 들어와야 하는 걸테고요..  정수기가 있으면 거기에 연결하면 되는데 저는 정수기 없어서 상판 대리석 잘 안 보이는 곳에 타공, 싱크대 밑에 연결했고 나중에 철거할 때를 여쭤보니 친절히 설명해주셨음. (그냥 똑 잘라서 묶어두면 된다고..)  +밑에 리뷰 작성하신 분, 왼쪽 오른쪽 틈 다른 건 이상 없는 거 맞습니다ㅎ 문이 잘 닫히고 물이 안 새면 정상 제품입니다~

Sentence (English): I had been using a SK Magic dishwasher for about 6 years, but suddenly there was a slight crack (1cm) on the bottom made of plastic.
Comments (English): I had been using a SK Magic dishwasher for about 6 years, but suddenly there was a slight crack (1cm) on the bottom made of plastic. I called A/S due to water leakage, and the repair technician asked for 200,000 won. I thought they were just trying to get me to buy a new product, so I gave up on after-sales service and washed the dishes by hand for several months, and as expected, I went straight to “dishwashing hell.” So, this time I purchased an LG product. After using it, there is nothing to complain about. As expected, LG is the best in home appliances. Everything is good except that the dishwasher door does not open automatically at the end of operation. It would be nice to have that function so that the water left on the dishes dries completely quickly, but that part is a bit disappointing. Anyway, starting today, I succeeded in escaping from “dishwashing hell” (it’s shortened to this these days)!
Comments (Original): 기존에 SK매직 식기세척기 6년정도 사용하고 있었는데, 갑자기 플라스틱으로 제작된 바닦쪽에 금이 살짝(1cm) 가서 누수현상으로 A/S를 불렀더니, 수리 기사님이 20만원 달라고 하셨습니다. 그냥 새 제품으로 사라고 유도하는 건가 싶어서 A/S 포기하고 몇 달간 손으로 설거지 했더니, 역시 '설거지 지옥'으로 직행.그래서, 이번엔 LG제품으로 구매했습니다. 사용해 보니 뭐~ 딱히 나무랄데가 없습니다. 역시 가전은 LG가 최고입니다.. 작동 종료하고 마지막에 세척기 문 자동으로 안 열리는 것 빼고 다 좋음. 그 기능이 있어야 식기에 남은 물기가 완벽하게 빨리 말라서 좋은데 그 부분은 조금 아쉽습니다. 하여튼, 오늘부터 '설거지옥' (요즘엔 줄여서 이렇게 말함. ㅋㅋ)에서 탈출 성공!

Sentence (English): Costco says this dishwasher comes with >$400 in savings, so at $900+, this dishwasher's full retail price puts it in the class between the second tier and top tier dishwashers from Bosch, LG, etc.
Comments (English): [ World's Okayest Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Costco says this dishwasher comes with >$400 in savings, so at $900+, this dishwasher's full retail price puts it in the class between the second tier and top tier dishwashers from Bosch, LG, etc. Unfortunately, aside from the clean look of the stainless steel door and stainless tub, this Dishwasher lacks almost all of the features of a high-end dishwasher. There's no digital readout of any kind, so you can't tell how long any wash cycle you choose will take, nor can you easily check to see how much time is left in your wash. There's no wifi or app connectivity, so there are no "wash finished" alerts or other useful features such as the ability to download a special cycle. When you need to run a load before dinner, or you're entertaining, this is an inconvenience. Most dishwashers these days have racks that allow you to lay down some or all of the rows and tines to allow for thicker items to fit in more easily. The LG I'm coming from allowed me to lay down any row or every-other tine in a row for both first and second level racks. This one has very little layout flexibility. The rows and tines are very tightly spaced and almost all are fixed in place and cannot be folded down. Only the last row of tines on the first rack folds down. The third row is designed to mostly hold coffee mugs or very short glasses and I haven't found anything my family actually uses that fits well in those spaces. Only 1/4 of that row holds long utensils like knives, tongs, etc. which is what a 3rd row is most useful for. Lastly, the wash arms look pretty flimsy and are simply plastic with a "stainless steel" silver finish on them. The one good thing I can say about this is that there is more room in the second row that I've had in other washers, and I can fit 20oz Hydroflask glasses upright without brushing the 3rd row. Overall, this feels like a basic Whirlpool dishwasher with a stainless steel bling package. For maybe 60% of the sales price, I might expect this, but I was expecting a $1400-class washer from a premium brand.

There's no digital readout of any kind, so you can't tell how long any wash cycle you choose will take, nor can you easily check to see how much time is left in your wash. There's no wifi or app connectivity, so there are no "wash finished" alerts or other useful features such as the ability to download a special cycle. When you need to run a load before dinner, or you're entertaining, this is an inconvenience. Most dishwashers these days have racks that allow you to lay down some or all of the rows and tines to allow for thicker items to fit in more easily. The LG I'm coming from allowed me to lay down any row or every-other tine in a row for both first and second level racks. This one has very little layout flexibility. The rows and tines are very tightly spaced and almost all are fixed in place and cannot be folded down. Only the last row of tines on the first rack folds down. The third row is designed to mostly hold coffee mugs or very short glasses and I haven't found anything my family actually uses that fits well in those spaces. Only 1/4 of that row holds long utensils like knives, tongs, etc. which is what a 3rd row is most useful for. Lastly, the wash arms look pretty flimsy and are simply plastic with a "stainless steel" silver finish on them. The one good thing I can say about this is that there is more room in the second row that I've had in other washers, and I can fit 20oz Hydroflask glasses upright without brushing the 3rd row. Overall, this feels like a basic Whirlpool dishwasher with a stainless steel bling package. For maybe 60% of the sales price, I might expect this, but I was expecting a $1400-class washer from a premium brand.

Sentence (English): Had this unit since Dec 2021 (it was the only dishwasher in stock back then).
Comments (English): [ great until you get the E1 F9 problem ] || ---------------- || Had this unit since Dec 2021 (it was the only dishwasher in stock back then). Overall, it was a reliable, quiet dishwasher; only used it ~3 days a week, and no major washings, except for holidays. But after 2.5 years, this past month it finally had issues [during wash cycle], specifically the E1 F9 alerts; had to reboot the machine to try to drain the water; sometimes it drained, sometimes not. Fortunately, I have a shopvac as backup. Note that this error happened sporadically, but after two weeks, I called our plumbers and was told I need new parts: control board, drain pump, and, because I had a slight leak (drip) in lower left corner of door assembly, a new gasket seal. Cheaper than buying a new unit, so I'm getting it serviced. Note that I've always used premium detergent (Cascade Platinum gel), but from what I've read online, several owners have reported this problem, all after 2 years of use, which apparently is the MTTF. Advise anyone considering purchasing this device to take that into consideration when choosing this model. Fwiw, I'm going to use Affresh to help minimize any possible lime/calcium buildup, although I doubt this caused problem(s).

Check the internet for more info from other owners, that's a sign you've got problems with pump(s), control board(s), or both. Lots of owners had issues after 2 years (MTTF). My tech had to get new pump(s), new control board(s), and because it has a slight leak on lower left corner, a new gasket(? ). Still cheaper than buying a new unit, but be advised.

Sentence (English): Bought this a month ago from Lowe's.
Comments (English): [ Works well but questionable build quality ] || ---------------- || Bought this a month ago from Lowe's. The package was carefully delivered and there were no visible signs of damage to the packaging. When I went to open the top and remove the foam I discovered that one of the top trim pieces on the left was hanging in a weird way. The one on the right was firmly in place. It looks like the cheap plastic construction of these trim pieces caused the tab holding it in place to snap off in shipping. That was my first introduction to this dishwasher. It appears to be contructed very poorly with cheaper components than what you would get in a lower price range even 7 years ago. I was able to resolve the issue without much hassle and Lowe's swapped out a new unit after 2 days. Installation was straightforward and now that I have been using it for the past while, it does a goo job of cleaning and drying the dishes without those stupid detergent gel packs getting stuck and not disolving like I was experiencing with my older unit. So far so good, but I don't expect this one to last as long as dishwashers from the past. We just have to get used to disposable appliances every 5 years or so.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher to replace a Whirlpool dishwasher that we had for 15 years.
Comments (English): [ Vertically Challenged ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher to replace a Whirlpool dishwasher that we had for 15 years. A huge selling point was the low decibels-- and it is VERY quiet. Over the past two months of using it, though, we have an issue we have yet to solve. It is this: The tines on the lower level back rack are too close together to fit anything but the flatest plates, and the tines in the front of the lower rack are too short to support serving bowls, gallon sized containers, or really anything more than a regular bowl. So things that can't be held firmly in place flip over and are filled with water. On the upper (middle) rack, the center is pretty much useless due to a hump running down it, and the spray is so powerful that it flips the smaller plastic drinking cups the kids use, and we're left with a cupful of dirty water. We even took a collection of bowls and plates to the store with us to confirm they'd fit, but we didn't think about the oddball items. The dishwasher cleans well, dries well, is easy to use, and is quiet. It just doesn't play nice with curvy objects.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher I had been using for a long time broke down, and since it was an old product, I couldn't get after-sales service, so I stopped using it for a few years and repurchased it.
Comments (English): [ I am very satisfied with the dishwasher because it has many convenient functions. ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher I had been using for a long time broke down, and since it was an old product, I couldn't get after-sales service, so I stopped using it for a few years and repurchased it. It's a new world to use a dishwasher after a long time. It washes and dries cleanly and is very convenient. I called the technician right after purchasing the product and set a visit date. He visited to check if the dishwasher could be installed, checked the renovation, and the two installers came back the next day. They were kind enough to thoroughly install the product and explain the dishwasher. This is my second time using a Samsung dishwasher. When I run it on standard washing, it washes and dries in 55 minutes. Since it has various functions, I think you can use it according to the situation. The size was enough for 12 people, even for a 5-person household that often eats home meals. If you look at the product details, it says that it is a dish basket optimized for Korean-style dishes. As described, I was able to use the space efficiently with air rice bowls and plates. It is also great that the door opens automatically after washing. I value ventilation, and it is convenient because it is automatic, so you don't have to check it separately and open it at the right time. I purchased a Samsung dishwasher that satisfies me in terms of installation, design, price, and functions!
Comments (Original): [ 식기세척기 기능이 다양하고 편리해서 넘 만족합니다. ] || ---------------- || 기존에 오랫동안 사용하던 식기세척기가  고장이 났는데 너무 오래전 제품이라서 AS가 불가로 세척기를 사용안하고 있다가  몇년만에 재구매를 했습니다.  오랫만에 식기세척기를 사용하니 신세계네요. 뽀득뽀득 알아서 잘 세척되고 건조까지  넘 편리합니다.  제품을 구매하고 바로 기사님께 전화가 와서 방문일을 정했어요.  식기세척기 설치 가능여부를 확인하기위해 방문하셔서 리폼 확인하시고 다음날 설치기사님 두 분께서 재방문하셨습니다. 꼼꼼하게 제품 설치완료와 세척기 설명까지 친절하셨습니다.  삼성 식기세척기는 두번째 사용해보는데요. 표준세탁으로 돌리니 55분만에 세척이랑  건조까지 금방 끝납니다.  기능이 다양하니 상황에 맞게 사용하시면  될 것 같아요. 사이즈는 집밥을 자주먹는 5인가구에도  12인용으로 충분했습니다.  제품 상세 설명란을 보면 한국형 식기에 최적화된  식기바구니라고 나와있는데요. 정말 설명대로 공간을 공기밥그릇이랑 접시를 효율적으로사용할 수 있었습니다.  세척이 끝나면 자동으로 문열림 기능까지 있어서  너무 좋네요.  환기를 중요시하는데 따로 확인하고 시간에 맞춰  열어줄 필요없이 자동으로 되어서 편리해요.  설치, 디자인, 가격, 기능까지 모두 만족스러운  삼성 식기세척기 구매입니다!

A good value and energy efficient machine.

Sentence (English): I had a Bosch 300 series for many years, so when it started to go (getting noisy and rinse adjent leaking) I knew I would get another Bosch.
Comments (English): [ Easier said than done ] || ---------------- || I had a Bosch 300 series for many years, so when it started to go (getting noisy and rinse adjent leaking) I knew I would get another Bosch. I was not intrested in any improvements/upgrades since I loved the Bosch I had. However, improvements and upgrades came with the 300 series weather I wanted them or not. I am not a fan of the touch buttons, I prefer a button I actually have to press. It was not intially easy to set up the Bosch with wifi which you have to do if you want to take advantage of the full options offered. The dishwasher just wouldn't connect. I had to walk away for a few days after using the machine to finally get it connected to the wifi. It's nice that you receive a message on your phone letting you know the dishes are sanitized and ready to unload, however, after a while the lights go out on the machine, and if you don't check your phone, you don't know the dishes are done. On the previous machine, the light on sanitized remained on so my husband always knew that the dishes in the machine were clean. What I do like alot is that third top rack! That is a big improvement and I love it! The machine is quiet and cleans well, so I am not sorry I bought another Bosch, so far.

I was not intrested in any improvements/upgrades since I loved the Bosch I had. However, improvements and upgrades came with the 300 series weather I wanted them or not. I am not a fan of the touch buttons, I prefer a button I actually have to press. It was not intially easy to set up the Bosch with wifi which you have to do if you want to take advantage of the full options offered. The dishwasher just wouldn't connect. I had to walk away for a few days after using the machine to finally get it connected to the wifi. It's nice that you receive a message on your phone letting you know the dishes are sanitized and ready to unload, however, after a while the lights go out on the machine, and if you don't check your phone, you don't know the dishes are done. On the previous machine, the light on sanitized remained on so my husband always knew that the dishes in the machine were clean. What I do like alot is that third top rack! That is a big improvement and I love it! The machine is quiet and cleans well, so I am not sorry I bought another Bosch, so far.

Sentence (English): I'm so bummed to give this dishwasher a so-so review.
Comments (English): [ High hopes were washed away.  ] || ---------------- || I'm so bummed to give this dishwasher a so-so review. I heard great things about Bosch dishwashers from a number of people, but I have been frustrated and disappointed by our dishwasher. Pros: 1. With the third shelf for silverware, I can fit a ton of dishes into this compared to my previous dishwasher. 2. When it runs, the dishes are very clean. 3. It is quiet. 4. It feels very solidly constructed. Not flimsy, lots of metal. Cons: 1. The soap dispenser door doesn't open when it runs. We just leave it open now. 2. There isn't a short/speedy cycle 3. The only way you can delay wash is through the app (or using your home's smart devices). I'd love to push a button on the appliance itself 4. The "clean" light indicator has never worked. Super problematic when you have kids whose chore is to unload the dishwasher. They've unloaded dirty dishes into the cabinets so many times. 5. When we do use the delay start feature with our Google Home system, it fails to run even though the Google system confirmed the run time. 6. If you don't have rinse-aid, it won't run and just loudly beeps. We have it on the lowest rinse-aid use setting and I feel like we have to add more really frequently.

Sentence (English): Finally, I got a dishwasher in my house!

Sentence (English): This unit replaced an Asko that had served me well for many years.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, roomy, fast ] || ---------------- || This unit replaced an Asko that had served me well for many years. I usually use the 1 hour cycle because the Asko delicate cycle had usually done the job for me, and that's been true of the Bosch. Internet connectivity is slightly useful, especially the reminder to add rinse agent. Less helpful was the reminder after one month to run a cleaning cycle with Bosch products that are not available in their online store, accompanied by an inscrutable red "check engine light" on the panel. The overall user interface is a bit weird: turn the power on, select your cycle, press start, possibly select some options, and now you have a few seconds to close the door or it will time out. There is slightly less vertical clearance on the bottom rack than I had with Asko, but it hasn't been an issue. There are plenty of customizable parts in the racks. A lot of reviews mention poor drying, and yes I notice some water in convex coffee mug bottoms, but it's not significant. The lack of a heater for drying is a bonus for putting plastic items such as food bowl lids in the top rack. My kitchen has white appliances and Bosch was one of the few high-end companies still producing them, so although it took a few extra weeks, I'm glad they're here.

I sincerely hope this new dishwasher lasts as long. On the plus side, it is extremely quiet. When we first got it, we turned it on and had to open the door to see if it was actually running. On the not-so-plus side, the old Bosch dishwaser would run a load in a mere 28 minutes, where the new one require 1:28 minutes to run an identical program. I understand that the Federal Government (EPA) has set almost impossible standards for dishwashers about how much water they are allowed to use and how hot the water can be, and manufactureres of dishwashers and dishwasher detergents (who have a whole other list of things they can and cannot do, thanks again EPA), but I am of the opinion that the cycle could be shortened considerably and the dishes would come out clean. In closeng, I am very pleased with the look and function of my Bosch dishwasher and hope to have many successful years using it.

In closeng, I am very pleased with the look and function of my Bosch dishwasher and hope to have many successful years using it.

Sentence (English): I changed my dishwasher from Samsung to LG because LG subscription was good, but I haven't been able to use it properly for a month after purchasing it.
Comments (English): I changed my dishwasher from Samsung to LG because LG subscription was good, but I haven't been able to use it properly for a month after purchasing it. The circuit breaker kept tripping at the beginning of the wash cycle, so I called a service call, but they only checked that there was no leakage in the cord while it was stopped, and said, "It must be a problem with the apartment wiring or the outlet, so there's nothing they can do," and left. After that, I changed all the multi-taps in the house, changed the outlet for the dishwasher and wired it separately, and called an electrician with my own money as well as the management office, and the result was, "There is no leakage anywhere in the house, and since the circuit breaker trips only at a certain point when the dishwasher starts, it is definitely a mechanical problem." I'm already worried whether they will properly handle it, such as replacing the machine, during the second service call scheduled for next week. It's hard to even schedule a repair date for the near future, so I made a reservation for next week, but I'm stressed out about how many times I have to leave work early and spend money and time because of the dishwasher. I even inquired about canceling my subscription because I was frustrated, but the cancellation fee is higher in the early stages, up to 900,000 won (I can't understand why I have to pay such a high fee even though I want to return it because it's no longer usable), and these days, I'm just getting more and more depressed without even being able to properly wash the dishes. Machines can break down at any time, and even if they're new, you might not receive a good product, but I thought that if it's an appliance subscription, the corresponding measures would be quicker and more detailed, but that doesn't seem to be the case, so I'm a bit cautious about recommending it to others.
Comments (Original): LG구독이 좋다하여 삼성에서 LG로 식기세척기 기변했는데, 구매해놓고 한 달 동안 제대로 사용을 못하고 있네요ㅜㅜ 세척 시작 초기에 차단기가 내려가는 현상이 반복되어 출장서비스를 불렀으나, 정지상태로 코드에 누전없음만 확인하고는 '아파트 배선이나 콘센트 문제일 것이니 해줄수 있는게 없다'하고는 철수... 이후 집에 멀티탭이란 멀티탭은 다 바꾸고, 식세기 콘센트를 바꾸면서 별도 배선으로 하고, 관리사무실은 물론 개인돈으로 전기기사까지 불러  확인한 결과 '집안 어디에도 누전은 없으며  식세기 작동 초기 특정 시점에만 차단기가 내려가는 것은 기계 이상이 분명하다'고 하는데... 과연 다음주로 예정된 2차 출장에서 기계 교체 등 제대로된 처리를 해줄지 벌써부터 걱정입니다ㅜㅜ 가까운 날짜에는 출장수리 일자도 잡기가 어려워 다음주로 예약했는데, 도대체 식기세척기 때문에 몇번이나 회사 조퇴를 하고 돈이며 시간을 써야할지 스트레스입니다... 답답한 마음에 구독해지 문의도 했었으나 초반일수록 위약금이 더 커 90만원 정도나 한다하니(사용이 안되서 반납을 하고자 하는데도 그렇게 고액을 내야하는 것도 납득이 안되긴 합니다만), 식기세척 한 번 제대로 못해보고 우울함만 쌓여가는 요즘입니다... 기계야 얼마든지 고장이 날 수도 있고 새것이라 해도 양품을 못받을 수도 있겠지만, 가전구독이라고 하면 그에따른 조치가 보다 신속하고 섬세할 것이라고 생각했는데 꼭 그렇지는 않은 것 같아 다른 분들에게 추천하기는 좀 조심스럽네요...

Comments (English): [ Possibly better than the 800 series?  ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) We bought this unit for the suite in our home at the same time we purchased an 800 series dishwasher for our main living area. I installed both units myself and was a bit surprised in the differences between the two units - with the scales being tipped in the favour of the cheaper model! The 300-series came with all the necessary parts, the 800-series needed me to purchase a water supply line and right-angle adapter fitting. The 300-series adjusts the METAL feet with an included metal wrench, unlike the 800 requiring a slot-head screwdriver to try and force the plastic feet to turn for leveling. The 300-series has a matching two-piece kick-plate to fully mask the bottom of the dishwasher, the 800 has a single-piece black kick. The 300-series has a better method of securing the unit to the cabinets with a metal bracket that clicks into the top of the dishwasher, AND has side-attach screws (if you are top-anchoring), whereas the 800 series uses a decades-old method of folding over a metal tab and ONLY secures with two screws. You'd think that the more expensive dishwasher would have the superior features, maybe it does when it comes to the programs and washing options, but the installation certainly plays a big part, and the 300 has it won, hands-down!

We'll see how they stack up in the long run to compare their lifespan and price for performance. Maybe my next unit won't be the higher-tier model.
